identity_assertions.normalized_value: South and south-central Texas: Hill Country (Edwards, Kinney, Val Verde, Kerr and neighbouring counties) and Coastal Bend (Nueces, Kleberg, Duval, Webb and neighbouring counties)

Multi-day flood system, Nov 7-9, 2026: flash flooding (life-threatening, Hill Country), river flooding forecast (Llano River crest 11.3 ft Nov 10; Oso Creek crest at flood stage), minor coastal flooding; NOT a severe convective event per SPC

evidence.raw_text_excerpt: Flash Flood Warning, NWS Austin/San Antonio TX, 7:46 PM CST Sun Nov 8 2026, extended (FF.W.0108) until midnight CST, for Edwards County, northwestern Kinney County and northeastern Val Verde County, south central Texas. At 7:46 PM CST, emergency management and TxDOT reports flooding across the warned area with several roads flooded and closed, including near US Highway 377, SH 55 and CR 450. A water rescue was reported this evening in the Newby Hills subdivision along CR 450. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have fallen over the past 24 to 36 hours. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible. HAZARD: Life threatening flash flooding. FLASH FLOOD DAMAGE THREAT: CONSIDERABLE. Locations include Rocksprings, Kickapoo Cavern State Park, Devils River State Natural Area and Pafford Crossing. Polygon LAT/LON points include 3029 10079, 3029 9985, 2951 10049, 2972 10115.

evidence.raw_text_excerpt: Excessive Rainfall Discussion, NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD, 2:31 PM EST Mon Nov 9 2026, Day 1 valid 16Z Mon Nov 09 - 12Z Tue Nov 10 2026. There is a Slight Risk of excessive rainfall across portions of far southeastern Texas. Numerous showers and thunderstorms continue across much of south-central and southern Texas. Any additional rain will fall on very saturated soils (NASA SPoRT-LIS 0-10 cm soil moisture >95th percentile region wide), leading to an isolated to scattered flash flooding threat at least into the early afternoon hours. Some areas have already seen 4-9 inches, especially within the zone between the southwestern side of Corpus Christi to about 50 miles east of Laredo. The area southwest of Corpus Christi near Kingsville was the epicentre of the heavy rain episode, with local totals ranging from 5-10 inches noted within observations and MRMS gauge-corrected data. Text as archived by the University of Illinois College of DuPage meteorology archive (kamala.cod.edu), a mirror of the NWS product.

evidence.raw_text_excerpt: Flood Warning for Oso Creek near Corpus Christi, Nueces County TX, as reproduced by Storm Station 247 from the NWS Corpus Christi product: moderate flooding is forecast; warning in effect until Tuesday evening. At 6:15 AM CST Monday the stage was 10.4 feet. Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. Forecast: the river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.0 feet just after midnight tonight, then fall below flood stage late tonight. Flood stage is 20.0 feet. At 20.0 feet, moderate lowland flooding occurs from the headwaters near Violet Road / Farm to Market 24 to Oso Bay. This is a secondary reproduction of an NWS product, not a direct fetch of the warning text in this build. Other same-day summaries of NWS products reported a crest near 23 feet late Monday night and a warning running longer (to Nov 11) - that difference is recorded as an open conflict, not resolved here.

signals.value: 10.48 ft gauge vs 10.4 ft warning stage

conflicts.description: No real property, owner, or matched counterpart estimate is attached; correlation cannot begin. By design in a public demo.

Oso Creek crest forecasts disagree between same-day summaries of NWS products: 20.0 ft just after midnight (warning reproduction, FL.W.0028) versus near 23 ft late Monday night in other summaries, with different warning end times (Tuesday evening vs Nov 11). The package does not pick a winner; a live run would have to re-fetch the current NWS product and use only that one.

Hazard classification conflict: SPC Day 1 (Nov 9) says NO severe thunderstorm areas forecast, while WPC/NWS flood products say flash and river flooding is occurring and forecast. Both are right about different hazards. This package classifies the event as FLOOD only; it must not be used as hail/wind/tornado or roof-damage evidence.

Temporal evolution, not a contradiction: the South Texas Flood Watch ran through noon CST Mon Nov 9 and was allowed to expire in the Corpus Christi afternoon discussion, while river flood warnings/forecasts (Oso Creek, Llano River crest Nov 10) continue after it. The globe view must show items with their own valid times, not one event window.
